**One month into Stackhouse Cloud, our library is still checking books out by hand**

Bridger Bend Community Library serves about 2,300 active cardholders from one branch, with two full-time staff and volunteers. We signed a three-year Stackhouse Cloud contract in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Our migration went live on October 19.

The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. The problem so far isn’t the product idea. It’s support—and the effect of unresolved problems on a small library’s daily work.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop. Our holds queue, which had around 640 holds, was wiped. We have an open support ticket that has been active for 12 days. We’ve received three replies, all saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering,” but we don’t yet have a resolution or a clear timeline.

That has real consequences for patrons. One retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he believed he had on hold. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home without the books. Meanwhile, one of our volunteers has been writing checkouts on index cards.

During the sales process, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” In practice, we got a shared inbox. For a library our size, that gap matters. We need to know who owns a serious migration problem and when we can expect an update.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library line item is on the agenda. I’m documenting this because commissioners and other libraries deserve an accurate picture of where things stand. This is one library’s experience, not a claim about every Stackhouse customer.

For now, I’m giving Stackhouse one star. I would revisit that rating if the company resolves the checkout and holds issues and improves communication. I’d also like a named senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week so we can agree on a recovery plan.

Other directors considering a contract: ask for support response times and migration responsibilities in writing before you sign. “Dedicated” should mean something specific when your patrons are counting on you.
